dedupe_keys.name: flanders care sector programme energy summer comfort and ventilation audits of care buildings to cut emissions and protect patients from heat belgium

description: This case describes how the Flemish government used building audits and subsidies to cut emissions from hospitals and care homes while protecting patients from heatwaves and airborne infection. It is published by Climate-ADAPT, the European Environment Agency's adaptation platform, with information from the Flemish Department of Care and the Flemish Energy Company. The programme covers some 8,000 care facilities in Flanders, from hospitals to elderly care homes and kindergartens. Its content: 2,673 energy audits, 112 summer comfort audits that simulated the thermal performance of buildings and proposed natural ventilation, envelope improvements and passive cooling, 378 ventilation audits launched during COVID-19, and a central platform holding audit data for 2,505 buildings to plan multi-year investments and track savings. It reports EUR 103 million of public investment from 2019 to 2025, 3,643 measures, 88,398 tonnes of CO2 and EUR 31 million of energy saved each year. The case is free and available to read online, with no data files to download. Caveats: results are reported by the programme owners, the audit data themselves are not published, and heat health outcomes are not quantified. Simulation uses: an example for sizing heat adaptation of care buildings, setting ventilation and cooling scenarios for hospitals, and appraising combined adaptation and energy investments. Related records: the Førde hospital flood protection (case_study-forde-hospital-flood-protection) and the New North Zealand hospital design (case_study-new-north-zealand-hospital-climate-adaptation) are other European hospital adaptation cases.
